title: Lacework
protagonist: Four women of the matric class of 1996 — and Lelethu Grace, the daughter they lost
logline: Thirty years after four schoolgirls swore a pact to hide a pregnancy and share a child, the child — now the most famous woman on the continent — walks into a Cape Town hotel suite with the DNA result already in her pocket. She knows who her mother is. What she wants to know is which of them decided.
blueprint: Shirley Conran, Lace (1982) engine: four school friends bound by a hidden pregnancy and a pact; the child given away and lost through a paid intermediary; the four women's working lives built in full procedural view across decades; the grown child, now famous, summoning them; the father whose position is what the secret protects. Maternity mystery retired (DNA killed it) and replaced by the anatomy of the pact; original cast, world, institutions and prose.
market: literary saga / four-women friendship epic / post-94 South Africa working-lives novel: craft exercise, not for commercial release
setting: South Africa — a Cape winelands girls' boarding school 1994–96; Johannesburg, Cape Town, Durban, London 1997–2026
sensitivity_read: REQUIRED — teenage pregnancy, informal adoption and the placement economy, exploitation of a minor in the entertainment industry, race and class in the first democratic school cohort. Indict the machine, never the people. See canon/MYTHOS.md.
